_comment: Canonical config for the local Qwen worker pipeline. Referenced by the MCP server (Phase 2+). Recorded at execution time 2026-06-30.

runner.notes: The sibling local-opencode supervisor exposes loopback OpenAI-compatible coding and embedding endpoints.

offload.notes: Qwen 3.8 uses the CUDA llama.cpp runtime. DeepSeek maps experts to CPU; Qwen Coder currently uses its compatible CPU-only runtime.
offload.vram_tight_policy: The supervisor loads one coding model at a time. Reduce configured context before changing the chosen quantization.

keep_alive._legacy_only: These values apply only to the legacy Ollama adapter. OpenCode/llama.cpp residency and idle unloading are controlled by the shared supervisor, not this block.
keep_alive.rationale: First request loads the model (~48 GB, cold ~55 s); requests within keep_alive reuse the resident model (warm ~0.1 s). Measured: 0.13 s warm load.
keep_alive.do_not_use_infinite: A warm model holds the whole GPU, which blocks other GPU work. 30m keeps it instant during a coding session but auto-unloads when idle so the GPU returns to other apps. GPU is taken in turns, not shared.

baseline_perf.note: Qwen Coder's compatible standalone runtime is CPU-only here. Qwen 3.8 is the faster default; model switches incur a cold load.

providers._comment: Workers the orchestrator can delegate to via delegate(provider=...). Built-ins: qwen/gemini/openai. ADD YOUR OWN WITHOUT CODE: any entry here with a known `kind` becomes a valid provider name — kinds: ollama-local (local Ollama), openai-compatible (OpenAI, Groq, OpenRouter, Mistral, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp server — set base_url/model/api_key_env), vertex-ai (Google Vertex). API keys NEVER go in config: name the env var in api_key_env. Optional per-provider `cost` (usd_per_mtok_in/out, flat or per model-tier) powers $ metering + usd budgets.

options._note: Passed to the OpenAI-compatible llama.cpp endpoint. LOW temperature is deliberate for deterministic code generation.

qwen._note: Default local worker through the shared llama.cpp supervisor.

qwen_coder._note: Opt-in 79.7B MoE coding model. The compatible standalone runtime is currently CPU-only.

options._note: Forwarded to GenerateContentConfig (temperature/top_p/max_output_tokens only). Low temperature for deterministic implement-to-spec output.

cost._note: Per model-tier prices in USD per MILLION tokens — set YOUR real Vertex prices in qwen.local.json (they change; 0 = unpriced, no $ metering). Powers est_cost_usd in metrics + the report, and metering.budgets.gemini_usd_per_day.

gemini._note: Two-tier Vertex worker (used by the `delegate` tool via google-genai). DO NOT put secrets/project/model-ids here — this file is committed. Set project, credentials_file (your Vertex service-account JSON), models.flash/pro (bare Vertex ids, e.g. gemini-2.5-pro), and enabled=true in config/qwen.local.json (gitignored). Copy config/qwen.local.example.json. The delegate/assign `model` arg picks 'flash' (routine) or 'pro' (hard) per task; empty = default_model.

openai._note: GPT/Codex via the OpenAI API. Set model (e.g. gpt-5.2-codex) — or a models tier map like gemini's — export OPENAI_API_KEY, then enabled=true in qwen.local.json. The same kind works for ANY OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Groq/OpenRouter/LM Studio/vLLM): copy this block under a new provider name and change base_url/api_key_env/model.

delegate._comment: Wave-2 token-cheap delegate options. context_max_*: caps for server-side context_files fetch. test_timeout_s: cap for the apply_to+test_cmd acceptance run. return_mode: default when the caller doesn't pass one ('full' returns code; 'summary' returns only the status footer — the code is on disk + in the output store).

retrieval._min_similarity_note: Cosine floor below which NOTHING is retrieved. top_k alone always returns the k least-bad matches, so an unrelated message ('hi') came back with k coding examples labelled 'past, SIMILAR tasks' and primed the agent to go do repo work. Measured on nomic-embed-text against this store: chit-chat peaks ~0.48, real coding requests start ~0.53. Raise it if the agent still cites irrelevant examples; lower it if it stops citing relevant ones.

gate._comment: §6.1 mechanical gate + worker->worker auto-retry. Runs entirely in-pipeline (no Claude tokens): checks a worker's output, and on failure bounces the verbatim error back to the worker up to max_retries times. Python is reliable in isolation; TS is off by default (snippets miss imports); C++ (UE) is deferred to the §9 host-harness (full builds too slow per-task).

python._note: Add "ruff" to checks to also lint (only fails if ruff is installed in the venv).

typescript._note: ON for SELF-CONTAINED TS (pinned typescript in package.json; invoked via `node`). `tsc --noEmit --strict` type-checks a standalone snippet in ms-to-seconds and catches real type errors. `--target ES2020` is REQUIRED: without it tsc defaults to ES5 and falsely rejects modern APIs (Number.isFinite, Math.trunc, Object.entries, optional chaining, …) that real projects use — set this to match your project's tsconfig `target`. The path is relative to the repo root; set an absolute path in config/qwen.local.json if the server's working directory differs. LIMITATION: a snippet that imports from a specific PROJECT won't resolve those imports → use `assign(...)` for project-coupled TS (its `done_when` is the project's OWN typecheck).

banned_patterns.message: FMath::Rand() is a non-crypto PRNG (weak low bits). For security-sensitive values (tokens/keys) use FGuid::NewGuid() or a CSPRNG.
Placeholder / incomplete body — the snippet looks unfinished.
New third-party dependency include — UE plugin must add NO new third-party deps; use engine APIs.

cpp._note: ON as a FAST (ms) heuristic lint ONLY — brace/paren balance (comment/string-aware), leaked-fence, and banned-pattern checks. It does NOT compile or type-check: an isolated C++ fragment can't resolve project/engine headers, and a full native build is too slow per-delegate. REAL C++ verification stays on the batched host-harness (see host_harness config) + the orchestrator's own review. banned_patterns is tunable — grow it from recurring corrections.

metering._comment: §6.5 per-delegation cost/outcome log -> metrics/metrics.jsonl (local, git-ignored). Report: `python src/metering.py [N]`. Claude token counts aren't visible to the pipeline; the tracked signal is machine-verified %% up and Claude step-ins down.

budgets._note: Per-provider daily ceilings since UTC midnight, from metrics.jsonl. 0 = no cap. ENFORCED: delegate/assign refuse a provider that is over budget (clear error → route to a local/free provider instead), and the §6.4 cascade skips escalating to an over-budget tier. Two styles per provider: <name>_tokens_per_day (tokens_out) and <name>_usd_per_day (needs providers.<name>.cost prices). Set real values in qwen.local.json once cloud spend matters.

agent._legacy_only: Fields below configure legacy Aider only. The default assign backend uses providers, opencode and workspace instead.
agent._comment: File-aware worker agents (Aider in a disposable git worktree). PROJECT-AGNOSTIC: the `assign` MCP tool takes repo=<abs path> + done_when=<shell cmd>, so it works on ANY git repo. Per-repo overrides via <repo>/.qwen-pipeline.json (its `agent` block merges over this). Set aider_exe to your isolated Aider venv's executable in config/qwen.local.json (e.g. .aider-venv/Scripts/aider.exe on Windows).

gemini._note: Used by the `assign` tool (Aider/litellm). model ids MUST use litellm's `vertex_ai/` prefix (service-account/ADC), e.g. `vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-pro` — NOT `gemini/` (that is the AI-Studio API-key path and ignores the service account). Fill models.flash/pro in config/qwen.local.json; the server injects GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS/VERTEXAI_PROJECT/VERTEXAI_LOCATION into env at call time from providers.gemini.

host_harness._comment: OPTIONAL, PROJECT-SPECIFIC batched build/test verify (NOT per-delegate). `python src/host_verify.py [--tests]` builds a host project and optionally runs its tests headless — a heavier 'Tier-2' check to run after a batch of native work / before commit. The example below is an Unreal Engine host project; set your real engine + project paths in config/qwen.local.json (gitignored) so this committed file stays portable. Leave empty to disable.

opencode._note: Coding runtime for chat/run/assign. Model catalog comes from providers. Local inference settings remain owned by the shared llama.cpp router.

agent_chat._opencode_note: OpenCode uses verify, test_cmd, test_timeout_s and use_corrections here. Other old loop/steering/compaction/escalation settings below apply to --backend legacy only. See docs/AGENT.md.
agent_chat._comment: The standalone coding agent (`apprentice chat` / `apprentice run`) — a conversational loop with file/search/edit/run tools, driven by ANY single provider (local or cloud). `verify` is the differentiator: after each turn the agent's changes are checked and REVERTED if they fail, with the verbatim error fed back to the model. off = plain agent (edits land immediately); gate = each edited file must pass the mechanical compile/lint gate; tests = gate + the project's own test command (degrades to gate if no test command is configured).
agent_chat._stream_note: Stream the model's reply token-by-token so long turns show progress instead of a dead pause. Supported for ollama-local and openai-compatible providers; vertex-ai replies arrive whole. Disable per provider with providers.<name>.stream=false.
agent_chat._note: allowed_cmds run without asking (prefix match, case-insensitive). denied_cmd_patterns are NEVER run (substring match) — the model cannot override them. Anything else asks the user first unless --yes. File paths are always confined to the target repo regardless of these lists.
agent_chat._escalation_note: After escalate_after_failed_verifies failed verifications the agent climbs cascade.ladder — cheapest rung first. Cloud tiers cost money, so the user is ASKED before each climb unless auto_escalate=true (headless runs always auto-approve). repeat_limit: after this many identical tool calls the agent is told to change approach. use_corrections: inject lessons from corrections/ into each turn.
agent_chat._parallel_note: Run independent READ-ONLY tool calls concurrently (models often ask for several files at once). Writes, commands needing approval, run_tests and finish always stay strictly ordered.

cascade._comment: §6.4 cost-ordered escalation. When the requested tier still FAILS the §6.1 mechanical gate after gate.max_retries, the pipeline escalates to `escalate_to` IF that provider is enabled (providers.<name>.enabled). Otherwise it falls through to Claude. Gemini is gated on creds today, so escalation is a no-op until providers.gemini.enabled=true. The 'front gate' (which tasks skip the cascade and go straight to Claude) is a Claude-side routing decision — see config/routing.md §6.
cascade._ladder_note: Ordered escalation path, cheapest first. Each rung is used only if that provider is enabled and under its daily budget. Add e.g. {"provider": "openai", "model": ""} to extend. Legacy escalate_to is the fallback when ladder is absent.
